rules.quoted_span: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this
rules.conflict_note: Division text as codified (3-2024); amended 2-27-2024 (effective 3-28-2024) and originally added 2004; the version setting the current just cause and relocation rules took effect 2023-06-24 (O-21647).
rules.interaction: Local just cause consistent with and additional to Cal. Civ. Code 1946.2; relocation paid is credited against other relocation owed under state or federal law.

all.unavailable: owner-occupied single-family or two-unit property, or separately alienable property with exempt-notice and non-corporate landlord

any.unavailable: deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing, hotel, mobilehome, care facility or dormitory

rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property with a tenancy over 30 days; applies from the first day of tenancy
rules.exemptions: housing with certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years; deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing (not Section 8); hotels and short-term rentals; mobilehomes under the Mobilehome Residency Law; care and transitional facilities; dormitories; shared kitchen/bath with resident landlord; owner-occupied single-family or two-unit property; separately alienable property owned by a non-REIT, non-corporate landlord with written notice
rules.key_value: no-fault relocation: 2 months' rent (3 months for senior/disabled)
rules.title: San Diego Residential Tenant Protections (Tenants' Right to Know), just cause and relocation
rules.requirement: A landlord may not end a tenancy without at-fault or no-fault just cause. For no-fault terminations the landlord must pay two months' rent (three if the tenant is a senior or disabled) or waive that amount of rent, regardless of income or tenancy length.

notes: San Diego Municipal Code ch. 9 art. 8 div. 7 (3-2024 edition). Division has no rent cap, deposit, screening or algorithmic provisions. Buyout, retaliation and remedies sections are outside the six categories.
